scope: Public kernel families on main, tracked at implementation-source granularity. Multiple public kernels may share one source file.
coveragePolicy: cargo llvm-cov line coverage is gated per crate against coverage-baseline.json (1.0 percentage point tolerance) by scripts/coverage_gate.py; see docs/verification.md. Coverage is visibility, not correctness evidence.
mutationPolicy: Every kernel's mutants are enumerated on each pull request and executed in full by the weekly advisory mutation-baseline workflow (cargo-mutants 27.1.0, .cargo/mutants.toml); see docs/mutation-testing.md. There is no score threshold or per-kernel triage of survivors yet, so every row records mutation as 'partial'.
benchmarkPolicy: 'benchmark' means a cargo bench target (Divan, Criterion or Iai-Callgrind) that exercises the kernel; wall-clock results are informational. Deterministic Iai-Callgrind and work/allocation gates are recorded under deterministicPerformance.

notes: oracleDifferential: This intentionally simple O(n^2) implementation is the correctness oracle for optimized broad phases.
benchmark: N/A. This O(n^2) reference is the correctness oracle the optimized broad phases are benchmarked against (bvh-kernels dynamic_pairs, octree boundary_cases); its own speed is not a contract.
runtimeProfiler: N/A. Reference oracle for the optimized broad phases, not a runtime path consumers profile.
benchmark: bvh-kernels dynamic_pairs and segment_queries (Divan).
Segment and box visits are checked against brute force over the live leaves; segment_queries is a Divan microbenchmark, not a deterministic sentinel.
benchmark: bvh-kernels segment_queries (Divan).
Finite generated scenes check root/child enclosure, exact leaf membership, input-order independence and pair parity with NaiveBroadPhase in tests/boundary_regressions.rs.
benchmark: New Divan boundary_cases benches measure normal/trace allocation cost for 64, 256 and 1024 bodies. The shared boundary evidence runner caps the 256-body control at 239 allocation calls.
benchmark: collection-kernels fenwick_tree (Divan).
deterministicPerformance: a unit test counts AddAssign calls and locks the 64-item linear build to 127 additions (fenwick-linear-build-64 in .performance/contract.json).
benchmark: collection-kernels lru_cache (Criterion).
runtimeProfiler: profiles/runtime-profiler/lru.json runs examples/profile_lru.rs (scripts/runtime-profile.sh lru).
benchmark: collection-kernels ring_buffer (Criterion).
benchmark: graph-kernels shortest_path (Criterion) measures dijkstra only; astar has no benchmark.
runtimeProfiler: profiles/runtime-profiler/traversal.json runs examples/profile_traversal.rs (scripts/runtime-profile.sh traversal).

SCCs: exhaustive four-vertex reachability oracle, deep chain/cycle subprocess on a 64 KiB stack, explicit seed ordering and test-only once-per-edge traversal counters. Topological-sort evidence is unchanged.
New SCC Divan workloads in benches/boundary_cases.rs cover chains, cycles and disconnected graphs at 64, 512 and 2048 vertices; no claim that heap frames universally improve latency.
benchmark: graph-kernels topology (Criterion) and boundary_cases (Divan, SCC).
benchmark: graph-kernels minimum_spanning (Criterion).
top_k_by: empty/short usize::MAX limits, unknown-length stable sort oracle and zero-limit nonconsumption; defined eight-result descending scans use at most 8n comparisons.
Divan boundary_cases measures exact/unknown-length streams and ordinary 4096-candidate selection; empty input must allocate zero times.
benchmark: search-kernels search and boundary_cases (Divan) plus performance_smoke (Iai-Callgrind).
runtimeProfiler: profiles/runtime-profiler/search.json runs quickselect in examples/profile_search.rs (scripts/runtime-profile.sh search).

deterministicPerformance: Iai-Callgrind sentinels quickselect-middle-4096, top-k-40-of-4096 and ranked-top-k-40-of-4096 plus the top-k-empty-oversized-limit allocation gate (.performance/contract.json).
benchmark: search-kernels search (Divan) and performance_smoke (Iai-Callgrind).
runtimeProfiler: profiles/runtime-profiler/search.json runs radix sort in examples/profile_search.rs (scripts/runtime-profile.sh search).
deterministicPerformance: Iai-Callgrind sentinel radix-sort-4096 in benches/performance_smoke.rs (.performance/contract.json).
oracleDifferential: The probabilistic contract is better expressed as no false negatives; exact false-positive equality is not an oracle contract.
benchmark: search-kernels performance_smoke (Iai-Callgrind bloom insert).
deterministicPerformance: Iai-Callgrind sentinel bloom-insert-4096 in benches/performance_smoke.rs (.performance/contract.json).

crates/statistics-kernels/tests/audit_regressions.rs checks finite extreme singleton/chunk merges, partition/reversal invariance and unbalanced counts; an internal test protects representable subnormal m2.

benchmark: New ordinary, extreme and chunk-count workloads use Divan in crates/statistics-kernels/benches/audit_numerics.rs; Cargo-native allocation regression tests and Divan benches reproduces overflow on the audited base.

tests/boundary_regressions.rs covers overflow-safe push, continued use after opposite finite extremes, push/merge agreement, non-finite rejection atomicity and bit-identical ordinary evaluation order. Divan boundary_cases compares ordinary/extreme push.

Scale-sweep sphere, OBB SAT and planar-adapter tests in crates/geometry-kernels/tests/audit_regressions.rs preserve outcome and trace parity; deterministic easy-sphere cases have an eight-iteration upper bound.

benchmark: New scaled GJK workloads use Divan in crates/geometry-kernels/benches/audit_numerics.rs; Cargo-native allocation regression tests and Divan benches keeps before/after outcomes separate from timings.
Analytic sphere/sphere and capsule/sphere distances plus diagonal AABB closest-corner distance provide independent oracle evidence.
Swapped-shape symmetry, touching/intersection classification, deterministic replay, and inconclusive-prepass refinement are covered.
benchmark: gap. No benchmark yet; one should be added once a consumer workload establishes representative hot-path shapes.

Prepared box frames own their immutable hull and match fresh preparation bit-for-bit across translation/margin changes without repeated vertex projections. Box/hull contacts: analytic signed face depths and finite-face witnesses, 512 deterministic rotated box/cube comparisons against the separate primitive SAT path, and the actual Greyhaven crate/panel Rapier oracle cover face/edge SAT and clipping. The contact kernel is not a sweep; Physics Engine still owns speculative response and CCD admission.
Analytic face, edge, corner and diagonal-corner-distance cases use a cube built with QuickHull. A deterministic 400-segment box-distance comparison exercises the physics-engine consumer.

A crossing/touching segment returns None so consumers retain a penetration-capable fallback. Translation invariance, deterministic work counters and AABB feature pruning have Cargo-native regression tests.
The Greyhaven static-rock Rapier oracle checks capsule cast timing and work on the real 32-point authored asset; wall-clock measurements are advisory outside controlled runners.

benchmark: geometry-kernels segment_hull_box (Divan) and performance_smoke (Iai-Callgrind box/hull contacts); the consumer's end-to-end oracle and deterministic feature-work counters remain the representative performance evidence.
benchmark: N/A. Inline fixed-size vector helpers with no algorithmic work of their own; their cost is measured inside every geometry benchmark that calls them.
runtimeProfiler: N/A. Inline vector helpers; a process-level runtime profile would only measure their callers.

crates/geometry-kernels/tests/audit_regressions.rs compares segment distance against independent convex one-dimensional minimization and covers scale, swap, reversal, crossing, skew, endpoint and capsule-oracle cases.
benchmark: New segment/capsule workloads use Divan in crates/geometry-kernels/benches/audit_numerics.rs instead of adding another Criterion suite.
crates/geometry-kernels/tests/audit_regressions.rs checks analytic support extrema and positive-direction rescaling from subnormal through overflow-prone finite vectors for spheres and capsules.
benchmark: New ordinary/extreme-direction workloads use Divan in crates/geometry-kernels/benches/audit_numerics.rs.
BVH contacts, sweeps and rays compared against unpruned triangle traversal; winding/translation, floor/ceiling/edge/initial-overlap/failure cases in triangle_mesh/tests.rs.

Box manifolds validate face, edge and corner witness membership, speculative Euclidean distance, rotations, two-sided winding, finite errors, deterministic replay and BVH-vs-unpruned queries in tests/box_mesh_manifold.rs.
Local-query doubling family asserts bounded exact triangle tests and logarithmic node visits; warm queries allocate nothing. Divan triangle_mesh bench separates preparation and query costs.

Capsule sweep searches triangles best-first by a lower bound on their touch (Newton time raised to a plane bound, shared with the heightfield sweep in sweep_search.rs) and stops at the best hit; a seeded differential fuzz (sweep_differential_tests.rs: 40000 sweeps over random closed caves, jittered grids with shared edges and vertices, and soups of thin and nearly degenerate triangles at offsets to 3e4; grazing and near-tangent displacements; 0..64 iterations) against the BVH-order kernel requires bit-identical Ok results, Err only where the old kernel failed with the same error, and every Err that became Ok to match the old kernel with 2^20 iterations. A work ratchet holds the cave sweep iterations below 80/50/90/55% of the old kernel (walk/fall/skim/fast diagonal); the Divan triangle_mesh bench times cave_capsule_sweep.
